2027-05-13.title: Seventh Thursday of Resurrection
2027-05-13.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: We declare to you the word of life
2027-05-13.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta), in the days between the Ascension and Pentecost. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and the Queen of Heaven (Regina Caeli) is prayed in place of the Angelus until Pentecost. The seventh day of the novena to the Holy Spirit. In the Latin calendar, Our Lady of Fatima (optional memorial), recalling the first apparition to three shepherd children at Fatima in Portugal on 13 May 1917.
2027-05-13.verse: Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
theo: The First Letter of John opens with a breathless sentence, the words of an old man who cannot forget what he saw as a young one: “We declare to you what was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we have looked at and touched with our hands, concerning the word of life.” Heard, seen, looked at, touched: four verbs piled one on another. John insists that the faith rests on a real encounter with a real person. The Word who was with the Father from the beginning became flesh, ate with fishermen, invited Thomas to put his hand into his side. “This life was revealed, and we have seen it and testify to it.” Now the Lord has ascended and is no longer seen in that way. How then do we meet him? John answers: through the witness of the apostles, handed on in the Church. “We declare to you what we have seen and heard so that you also may have fellowship with us; and truly our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.” The chain is clear: the apostles saw; they declared; we who hear them enter into fellowship with them, and through them with the Father and the Son. Our Church received that witness from Thomas, the apostle who touched the wounds. In these days before Pentecost, the Spirit is preparing the apostles to begin declaring.

The Gospel shows what that fellowship costs. “Now large crowds were traveling with him; and he turned and said to them, ‘Whoever comes to me and does not hate father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, yes, and even life itself, cannot be my disciple.’” The word “hate” shocks us. In the language of the Bible it is a way of saying “prefer less”; Matthew gives the same saying as “Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me” (Matthew 10:37). Jesus is not asking us to stop loving our families; he who gave us the commandment to honour father and mother asks that no love, not even the dearest, take his place. Then he speaks plainly: “Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.” A crowd follows for a day; a disciple follows to the end.

Jesus gives two little parables of good sense. A man who wants to build a tower first sits down and estimates the cost, so that he is not mocked: “This fellow began to build and was not able to finish.” A king going to war with ten thousand against twenty thousand first sits down and considers whether he can win. Both sit down before they begin. Discipleship is not an enthusiasm of one evening; it is a decision taken with open eyes. “So therefore, none of you can become my disciple if you do not give up all your possessions.” Finally he speaks of salt: “Salt is good; but if salt has lost its taste, how can its saltiness be restored?” A disciple who has stopped paying the cost loses his flavour. Many in Kerala know what that means: families where the faith has become only a custom, where the name is Christian but the taste is gone. Salt, Leviticus says, was offered with every sacrifice as “the salt of the covenant” (Leviticus 2:13). Today the Latin Church remembers Our Lady of Fatima, who asked three poor children to pray, to do penance and to offer sacrifices for sinners. Mary is the disciple who counted the cost at Nazareth and paid it at the foot of the Cross. In the upper room she prayed for the Spirit who alone can give us the courage to finish the tower we have begun.
conn: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God” (John 1:1); “the Word became flesh and lived among us” (John 1:14).
The Risen Lord says, “Touch me and see; for a ghost does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have” (Luke 24:39).
“Put your finger here and see my hands. Reach out your hand and put it in my side” (John 20:27).
“Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me” (Matthew 10:37).
“Where you go, I will go; where you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God” (Ruth 1:16).
“You are the salt of the earth; but if salt has lost its taste, how can its saltiness be restored?” (Matthew 5:13).
altar: The Word of life whom the apostles touched is placed in our hands at every Holy Qurbana. We too can say: we have received, we have touched, we have tasted. Our fellowship at the altar is fellowship with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.
At the altar Christ carries his Cross to the end and offers himself fully; there we receive strength to carry our own cross and to keep the salt of our faith from losing its taste.
outline: An old apostle who cannot forget what he heard, saw and touched.
Heard, seen, touched: the witness handed on to us from Thomas.

live: Tell one person this week, simply, what Jesus has done in your life.
Look at one family duty or affection that has pushed God aside, and give God his place again, without loving your family less.
Choose one Christian commitment you have started and left half done, and decide how to finish it.
Restore one practice that has lost its taste in your home: family prayer, Sunday Qurbana, grace before meals.
Pray the rosary today for the conversion of sinners and for peace, as Our Lady asked the children at Fatima.
fathers: What does John mean when he says, our hands have touched the Word of life? Can anyone touch the Word with his hands? But because the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, the Word who could not be touched became touchable. Through those who touched him we too have come to him.

The disciples are called salt not for their own sake but for the whole earth. Salt does not preserve itself; it preserves what it touches. If the salt loses its strength, it cannot preserve others, and it is fit only to be thrown away. So the Christian lives not for himself but to keep the world from corruption.
magis: The transmission of the Christian faith consists primarily in proclaiming Jesus Christ in order to lead others to faith in him. From the beginning, the first disciples burned with the desire to proclaim Christ: “We cannot but speak of what we have seen and heard.”
Family ties are important but not absolute. The first vocation of the Christian is to follow Jesus: “He who loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me.”
Conversion is accomplished in daily life by gestures of reconciliation, care for the poor and the defence of justice; taking up one's cross each day and following Jesus is the surest way of penance.
The People of God has for its mission to be salt of the earth and light of the world.
Private revelations, recognised by the Church, do not improve or complete Christ's definitive Revelation, but help us to live it more fully in a certain period of history.
saints: 7–13 May: the days after the Ascension of our Lord (Thursday 6 May), when the apostles waited in prayer for the Holy Spirit “together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus” (Acts 1:14). Many families and parishes pray a novena to the Holy Spirit from Friday 7 to Saturday 15 May, the eve of Pentecost. Fri 7: First Friday. Sun 9: Seventh Sunday of Resurrection, the Sunday after the Ascension; the Latin Church in India celebrates the Ascension on this Sunday. Mon 10: in the Latin calendar, St John of Avila. Wed 12: in the Latin calendar, Sts Nereus and Achilleus and St Pancras. Thu 13: in the Latin calendar, Our Lady of Fatima. The Marian month of May continues (verify locally).
2027-05-13.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Word of life, you were heard, seen and touched by your apostles, and through their witness we have fellowship with the Father and with you. Give us the courage to put you before every other love, to carry our cross and follow you to the end. Teach us to count the cost and to finish what we have begun, and keep the salt of our faith from losing its taste. Through the prayers of the Virgin Mary, who paid the cost of discipleship at the foot of the Cross and prayed with the apostles for the Spirit, send us your Holy Spirit. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: John: we declare to you what we have heard, seen and touched, the word of life, so that you may have fellowship with us and with the Father and the Son.
Jesus: whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple; no love may take his place.
Count the cost like the builder and the king; salt that loses its taste is thrown away.
2027-05-13.action: Finish one Christian commitment you have left half done, and restore one family practice that has lost its taste.
2027-05-13.question: Am I a member of the crowd that follows for a day, or a disciple who follows to the end?
catechism: Witness to what we have seen and heard.
Family ties and the first vocation.
kidsaint: Francisco and Jacinta were a brother and sister from a poor village near Fatima in Portugal. On 13 May 1917, while they were looking after sheep with their cousin Lucia, Our Lady appeared to them and asked them to pray the rosary every day and to make little sacrifices for sinners. They did it with all their heart, even when people did not believe them. Both died young, Francisco in 1919 and Jacinta in 1920, and Pope Francis declared them saints at Fatima on 13 May 2017. Lesson: even children can pray and offer sacrifices for the world.
2027-05-13.special: Seventh Thursday of Resurrection. Seventh day of the novena to the Holy Spirit. In the Latin calendar, Our Lady of Fatima.
term: The Greek word koinonia means sharing, communion, having something in common. John uses it for the life the apostles share with the Father and the Son, and which they open to all who receive their witness (1 John 1:3). The first believers in Jerusalem “devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers” (Acts 2:42). It is the communion of the Church, made by the Holy Spirit.

family.explain: Jesus said that following him is like building a tall tower. Before you start, you sit down and think: do I have enough bricks and money to finish it? Otherwise people will laugh: ‘He started but could not finish!’ Jesus wants us to follow him all the way, even when it is hard, like carrying a cross. The Holy Spirit gives us the strength to keep going.
family.intention: We pray for people who started following Jesus and have stopped, that they may come back.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there a good thing we started as a family and did not finish? Let us finish it!”

illus: On a roadside near Thodupuzha there stands a house that was never finished. The pillars of the first floor rise into the sky with their iron rods rusting in the rain, and grass grows on the roof slab. Neighbours say that the owner began to build it with great plans and a loan he could not repay. Every child who passes asks the same question: ‘Who started that house?’ Jesus said that discipleship is like that: it is easy to lay a foundation in a moment of enthusiasm, at a retreat, on the day of First Holy Communion, and much harder to build to the roof. The Holy Spirit is given to the Church so that the towers we begin may be finished.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Word of life, we have heard of you and received you. Gather us in fellowship with the Father and with you, and give us courage to follow you to the end. Amen. Alleluia!
share: What we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we have looked at and touched with our hands (1 John 1:1). How have I “touched” the Lord in my life?
Whoever comes to me and does not hate father and mother … cannot be my disciple (Luke 14:26). Is any love in my life taking the place of Christ?
Which of you, intending to build a tower, does not first sit down and estimate the cost? (Luke 14:28). What Christian commitment have I started and not finished?
Salt is good; but if salt has lost its taste, how can its saltiness be restored? (Luke 14:34). Where has my faith lost its taste?
pm.resp: Lord, give us strength to follow you to the end.
interc: For the Church, that she may declare with joy what the apostles saw and heard.
For those who have lost the taste of faith, that the Spirit may renew them.
For families, that they may love one another deeply and love Christ above all.
For peace in the world and the conversion of sinners, as Our Lady asked at Fatima.
For children and young people, that like Francisco and Jacinta they may pray generously.
pm.close: Father, through the witness of the apostles you have called us into fellowship with you and your Son. Give us the Spirit, that we may carry our cross, finish what we have begun and be salt for the earth, through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, the First Letter of John begins with an old apostle's memory: “what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we have looked at and touched with our hands, concerning the word of life.” John had touched Jesus. Our faith rests on a real meeting with a real person.

Now the Lord has ascended. How do we meet him? Through the witness of the apostles, handed on in the Church. “We declare to you what we have seen and heard so that you also may have fellowship with us.” We received this witness from St Thomas, who touched the Lord's wounds.

In the Gospel, large crowds follow Jesus. He turns and says: unless you put me before father and mother, before even your own life, you cannot be my disciple. He does not ask us to love our families less, but to love him most. “Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.” A crowd follows for a day; a disciple follows to the end.

Jesus speaks of a man who builds a tower without counting the cost, and cannot finish. Many of us have begun towers: a promise at a retreat, a resolution after confession. Let us finish them. And he speaks of salt that loses its taste. Faith that becomes only a habit loses its taste. Let us restore it.

Today the Latin Church remembers Our Lady of Fatima. Mary asked three children to pray and offer sacrifices. She herself counted the cost at Nazareth and paid it at the Cross. In the upper room she prayed for the Spirit. Let us ask her to pray for us, that the Spirit may give us courage to follow to the end. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: before you build a big tower, think if you can finish it! Following Jesus is like building a tower: we must keep going even when it is hard.
At Fatima, Mary asked three children to pray every day. You can pray too! Today, say a Hail Mary for someone who is far from Jesus.

intro: Theme: “Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.”
The seventh day of the novena: the word of life heard, seen and touched, the cost of following Christ to the end, and the salt that must not lose its taste.

sub: Fellowship with the Father and the Son.
q: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
We declare to you what was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we have looked at and touched with our hands, concerning the word of life.
points.apply: Tell one person this week, simply, what Jesus has done in your life.

points.h: Carry the cross and follow me
sub: No love in the place of Christ.
q: Do not press me to leave you or to turn back from following you! Where you go, I will go; where you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
points.apply: Give God back his first place in one area where another love has pushed him aside.

points.h: Sit down and count the cost
q: You shall not omit from your grain offerings the salt of the covenant with your God; with all your offerings you shall offer salt.
Salt is good; but if salt has lost its taste, how can its saltiness be restored?
points.apply: Finish one Christian commitment you have left half done, and restore one family practice of prayer.

concl: The apostles touched the Word of life and handed him on to us; the Spirit gives us courage to follow him to the end.
With Mary, who paid the cost at the Cross, let us carry our cross and keep our salt.
2027-05-13.resolve: This week, bear witness once, put Christ first in one thing, finish one tower, and pray the rosary for peace.
